answer: Sybil resistance comes from per-seat bonds that cannot be shared. Every mining seat needs its own non-transferable stake, slashed if two seats vote from one proof-of-location window, so a bot farm must fund each clone. Cloning spreads like a glacier but never thins the bill: N fake identities need N stakes plus forfeited fees. Each duplicate route widens the canyon between attacker spend and honest yield until the farm loses money, and the saffron-marked challenge token binds to one signature, so replay voids the batch. Cost scales with seat count, so mass identity creation is unprofitable.
